summary: Eleven concrete, comment-endorsed tools, books, and technical resources surfaced from a complete HN front-page comment crawl.
telegram_footer: 11 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: comment-fmt
items.source_story_title: Claudette: Make Claude stop talking like a BuzzFeed article
items.summary: A deterministic formatter and linter for source-code comments.
items.why_included: Its author uses it in CI to reserve agent-review time for actual behavior.
items.evidence: The author said they run its formatter and linter across all personal projects.

evidence_sources.author: vilos1611
evidence_sources.excerpt: Both with a formatter and a linter that I run in CI for all my personal projects.

items.name: Pocket TTS
items.source_story_title: How we made a text-to-speech model respond in sub-50 ms
items.summary: A compact text-to-speech model designed for fast CPU inference.
items.why_included: A voice-assistant builder praised its speed after evaluating many TTS options.
items.evidence: The commenter reported actively using Pocket TTS and called it super fast.

evidence_sources.author: armcat
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've now been using Pocket TTS which is super fast

items.name: Legacy Survey Sky Viewer
items.source_story_title: Scientists release biggest 2D map of the universe
items.summary: An interactive browser viewer for astronomical survey imagery.
items.why_included: A commenter enthusiastically surfaced it as an app-like way to explore space.
items.evidence: The commenter linked the viewer and called it cool.

evidence_sources.author: sans_souse
evidence_sources.excerpt: Oh this is cool! Google Space could soon be an app :) https://viewer.legacysurvey.org/

items.name: Web Platform Dashboard
items.source_story_title: Small, native web tricks worth remembering
items.summary: A dashboard tracking browser support for web-platform features.
items.why_included: A commenter recommended it alongside established references MDN and Can I Use.
items.evidence: The commenter explicitly added Web Platform Dashboard to a list of great web references.

evidence_sources.author: chrisweekly
evidence_sources.excerpt: MDN and caniuse.com are great. See also https://webstatus.dev

items.name: Baseline
items.source_story_title: Small, native web tricks worth remembering
items.summary: A compatibility standard showing when web features are broadly available.
items.why_included: A commenter recommended it with trusted browser-support references.
items.evidence: The commenter included Baseline in a concise list of useful web-platform resources.

items.name: Ascension by Oliver Harris
items.source_story_title: I accidentally logged hundreds of thousands of phone calls to military bases
items.summary: A contemporary spy novel set on remote Ascension Island.
items.why_included: A commenter directly recommended it as a really great spy novel.
items.evidence: The recommendation connected the novel's unusual setting to the thread's subject.

evidence_sources.author: shorsher
evidence_sources.excerpt: There's a really great spy novel that takes places there, Ascension by Oliver Harris.

items.name: Software Engineering at Google
items.summary: A free online book about engineering practices for long-lived codebases.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly said the freely available book is worth reading.
items.evidence: The commenter linked the complete online edition and endorsed it.

evidence_sources.author: tmoertel
evidence_sources.excerpt: It's available online for free: https://abseil.io/resources/swe-book And, yep, it's worth a read.

items.name: The Best Short Stories of J.G. Ballard
items.source_story_title: New Worlds: We are living in the future of J.G. Ballard or William Gibson
items.summary: A collection showcasing J.G. Ballard's short science-fiction work.
items.why_included: A commenter named it as their favorite Ballard collection.
items.evidence: The commenter said the collection contains some of Ballard's best science fiction.

evidence_sources.author: jlarocco
evidence_sources.excerpt: My favorite is "The Best Short Stories of J.G. Ballard". It has some of his best sci-fi, and they're all under 50 pages.

items.name: What Every Programmer Should Know About Memory
items.source_story_title: What happens when a GPU reads memory
items.summary: A deep technical guide to memory hardware and software performance.
items.why_included: A commenter invoked it as a very good companion to the submitted article.
items.evidence: The commenter strongly endorsed the article while linking a copy.

evidence_sources.author: KellyCriterion
evidence_sources.excerpt: VERY good article, reminds me on: "what every programmer should know about memory"

items.name: Architecture of Consoles
items.source_story_title: What happens when a GPU reads memory
items.summary: Illustrated technical analyses of video-game console architectures.
items.why_included: A commenter described Copetti's articles as rewarding technical rabbit holes.
items.evidence: The commenter said the series builds a useful high-level understanding through deep exploration.

evidence_sources.author: nazgulsenpai
evidence_sources.excerpt: I noticed this the first time on copetti.org articles about game console architectures: know nothing, look every jargon or acronym up as you read along, end up with 42 tabs and a basic high-level understanding of the topic by the end.

items.name: Kobo Clara HD
items.summary: A compact six-inch E Ink reader with adjustable front lighting.
items.why_included: An eight-year owner still called it a great device.
items.evidence: The commenter reported long-term use and clear satisfaction.

evidence_sources.author: jcul
evidence_sources.excerpt: I'm still using my kobo clara hd that I bought 8 years ago. What a great device.
